runs.t: •  Say: It's on May 5th. It's in May.

slides.notes:
Welcome. Say: "Today: dates and the weather." Point to the calendar: "May 5th."
Before class: print the Student Pages (number expected + 3 spares), one set of picture cards per group of 3–4, the appointment cards for Talk Time, and the ordinals card (1st–5th…). Have the phone + small speaker and L1_L9_listening.mp3 ready. Prep time: 30 min.
No holidays: never ask about religious or cultural holidays. Invented birthdays are fine.
Teach in English. Show, point, and gesture. Say less, show more.
Class plan: 6:00 Hello + Review, 6:10 New Words, 6:20 Listening, 6:32 Grammar, 6:45 Break, 7:00 Talk Time, 7:10 Exit Ticket + Homework, 7:15 Real-World Reading, 7:25 Progress Check.
Source: level1_curriculum/lesson9/Level1_Lesson9.md (At a glance, Clock-time plan, Teacher notes).

slides.title: What's the Date?

runs.t: I can say and write a date.
I can use in, on, at.
I can read an appointment card.

slides.notes:
Click to show each goal, one at a time. Read it aloud. Learners repeat.
Goal 1: say the months and write a date: May 5th / 5/5.
Goal 2: "When is your birthday?" "It's on May 5th." / "It's in May."
Goal 3: in + month, on + date or day, at + time.
Goal 4: "How's the weather?" "It's cold / hot / sunny / rainy."
Goal 5: understand an appointment day and time; read a simple appointment card (Real-World Reading at 7:15).
Source: level1_curriculum/lesson9/Level1_Lesson9.md (At a glance: Objectives).
slides.title: Today's Goals

runs.t: What do you want for lunch?

slides.notes:
Pairs. 15 learners: 7 pairs + 1 group of 3. 7–8 learners: 3–4 pairs. Late arrivals join any pair.
Before class, write on the board: Do you like fish? What do you want for lunch? What day is today?
Model with one learner: "Do you like fish?" "Yes, I do." Then "What day is today?"
Click to show the A question. Click again for the B answers. Pairs use the Hello + Review page: 1 Do you like fish? 2 What do you want for lunch? I want ___. 3 What day is today? It's ___. Switch. Then find a new partner.
Homework check (last 3 min): partners show last week's homework. Walk around and look.
New learners: pair them with a strong partner. If behind: one partner only.
Source: level1_curriculum/lesson9/Level1_Lesson9.md (Step 1: Hello + Review; Student Pages: Hello + Review).

runs.t: Thursday, May tenth, at ten thirty.

slides.notes:
Before you listen (1 min). Say: "Kim calls the clinic. She makes an appointment. Then Kim and Marco talk about the weather and birthdays."
Click to show each listen. Listen 1: Task A (the appointment: day, date, time). Listen 2: Task B (circle the weather). Listen 3: Task C (write the birthdays).
Say it!: read each line. Learners repeat: "Thursday, May tenth, at ten thirty." "How's the weather?"
The audio L1_L9_listening.mp3 (about 1:10) plays the conversation once. Press play again for the next listen. Pairs compare after each task. Write answers on the board.
No speaker? Read the script with a volunteer. Say dates as words: May tenth, May fifth, ten thirty.
Voices: Narrator, Receptionist, Kim, Marco. Synthetic voices made with Chatterbox TTS (MIT), copied from short reference clips made with Kokoro-82M (Apache 2.0); no recordings of real people. Riverside Clinic is invented.
If behind: play 2 times; do Task C together.
Source: level1_curriculum/lesson9/Level1_Lesson9.md (Step 3: Listening; Listening script).

runs.t: Part one. Kim calls the clinic.

slides.notes:

Pairs compare. Then click to show each answer: Thursday; May 10; 10:30 (in the morning).
In the audio: "How about Thursday, May tenth, at ten thirty?" "Is that in the morning?" "Yes, it is."

runs.t: Part two. Kim and Marco talk.

slides.notes:
Listen 2 (Task B): learners circle the weather. Listen 3 (Task C): learners write the birthdays of Marco and Kim.
Pairs compare. Then click to show each answer.
Task B: sunny, hot ("It's sunny and hot. I like sunny days.").
Task C: Marco: May 5th ("It's on May fifth. Next week!"). Kim: October ("My birthday is in October.").
If behind: play the audio 2 times, and do Task C together.

slides.notes:

Box 1: "What's the date today?" Click: "It's October 20th." Box 2: "When is your birthday?" Click: "It's on May 5th." / "It's in May."
Click to show each answer. Learners repeat the question and the answer.
Write on the board: on + date or day; in + month. Months always start with a capital letter.
Check questions: "My birthday is ___ May." (in) • "My birthday is ___ May 5th." (on)

slides.title: What's the date?

slides.notes:
Box 3: "When is your appointment?" Click: "It's on Tuesday, at 3:00." at + time.
Then click: in, on, or at? in + month (in May). on + date or day (on May 5th, on Tuesday). at + time (at 3:00).
Check question: "Class is ___ 6:00." (at)
Big mistake this week: in May 5th / at May. Point to Grammar Box 2.
Source: level1_curriculum/lesson9/Level1_Lesson9.md (Step 4: Grammar Q&A, Box 3; Grammar Box 3; Questions and answers; Teacher notes).

slides.title: When is your appointment?

slides.notes:
Box 4: "How's the weather?" "It's sunny / rainy / cold / hot." Point out the window. Learners answer.
Read each DON'T SAY line. Shake your head. Click to show the SAY line. Learners repeat it.
Weather: It's cold (not It makes cold). For people: I'm cold. Cross out It makes cold on the board.
Pair drill (last 3–4 min): A asks birthday / appointment / weather; B answers; switch. If behind: skip the pair drill; Talk Time practices the same language.
Source: level1_curriculum/lesson9/Level1_Lesson9.md (Step 4: Grammar Q&A, Box 4 and pair drill; Grammar Box 4; Common mistakes; Teacher notes).
slides.title: How's the weather?

slides.notes:
How do I write a date in the U.S.? Month / day / year. Ask: "In the U.S., 5/10 is…?" Click: "May 10 (not October 5)."
Right box: "Do months start with a capital letter?" Click: "Yes. May, October (always)."
Ordinals 1st–31st: teach with the card. Say: first, second, third, fourth, fifth.
Spanish speakers: in the U.S. the date is month/day/year (5/10 = 10 de mayo). Learners can read the Spanish note on their Grammar page.
Source: level1_curriculum/lesson9/Level1_Lesson9.md (Grammar: Questions and answers; Teacher notes).

runs.t: Write in, on, at, or a weather word.

slides.notes:
Learners write in, on, at, or a weather word on lines 1–5. Then pairs check.
Click to show each answer: 1 on, 2 in, 3 at, 4 sunny (or rainy / cold / hot), 5 on (on + day).
Line 6 on the page: write today's date (answers will vary).
Source: level1_curriculum/lesson9/Level1_Lesson9.md (Grammar: Practice; Answer key, Grammar practice; Questions and answers).
slides.title: in, on, at?

slides.notes:
Read each "Don't say" line. Shake your head. Click to show the correct line. Learners repeat it.
It makes cold → It's cold. I have cold → I'm cold. / It's cold.
in May 5th → on May 5th (on + date). at May → in May (in + month).
Tip: read the grammar boxes left to right. Copy one question and one answer.
Source: level1_curriculum/lesson9/Level1_Lesson9.md (Grammar: Common mistakes; Teacher notes).

slides.title: Talk Time

slides.notes:
Part 2, appointment (5 min). A–B pairs. A = receptionist with the appointment card (Thursday, May 10, 10:30). B = patient. Then switch.
Model it: "When is my appointment?" Click: "On Thursday, at 10:30."
A says: "Your appointment is on ___, at ___." B repeats: "On ___, at ___. OK. Thank you!" B writes the day, the date, and the time. B can also ask "What time?"
If behind: one round only.
Source: level1_curriculum/lesson9/Level1_Lesson9.md (Step 5: Talk Time, Part 2; Student Pages: Talk Time, Appointment A and B).
slides.title: Appointment

slides.notes:
Exit ticket (never skip): each learner says "My birthday is in ___." or "It's on ___." Copying from the box is fine.
Homework (10 minutes): open the Homework page. Do item 1, line 1 together. Point to each instruction.
Homework: 1) write: Today is… Tomorrow is… My birthday is… How's the weather today?; 2) write in, on, or at; 3) write 3 months and say them to a family member or a friend; 4) look at a calendar and write today's date two ways (words and month/day/year); 5) review: write one food you like (Lesson 8).
Homework answers: item 2: 1 in (October), 2 on (Monday), 3 at (7:00), 4 on (May 5th).
Source: level1_curriculum/lesson9/Level1_Lesson9.md (Step 6: Exit Ticket + Homework; Student Pages: Homework; Answer key).

slides.title: Read the Card

slides.notes:
Read it (4 min), Task B: U.S. date order is month / day / year. 5/10 = May 10.
Learners match each date to a, b, or c. Then click to show each answer: 5/10 → b May 10; 10/5 → a October 5; 12/25 → c December 25.
If behind: do Tasks A and B only.
Source: level1_curriculum/lesson9/Level1_Lesson9.md (Real-World Reading step; Student Pages: Real-World Reading B; Answer key, Real-World Reading B).
slides.title: U.S. Dates

slides.notes:
Task C: learners write today's date two ways: words and numbers (month/day/year). Answers vary.
Task D (pairs): A says a date from Task B; B points. Then switch. Partners: A is the receptionist, B repeats the appointment.
Click to show how to say each date. Learners repeat: May tenth, October fifth, December twenty-fifth.
Source: level1_curriculum/lesson9/Level1_Lesson9.md (Real-World Reading step; Student Pages: Real-World Reading C and D).
slides.title: Say the Date

slides.notes:
Progress Check (5 min). Individuals. Open the Progress Check page.
Part A: read each item slowly, 2 times: 1 May, 2 sunny, 3 10:30, 4 cold, 5 today. Learners circle.
Parts B and C: learners match and write on their own. Help with the instructions only. Click to show the Part B answers when you check together: 1 b, 2 a, 3 c, 4 d.
Part C answers: 1 in (June), 2 on (Friday), 3 at (9:00), 4 on (May 10th).
Part D: read each "I can…" line and point to the 3 faces. Learners check one.
Score: A /5 + B /4 + C /4 = /13. Not a test grade. Collect if you want. If behind: do it next week at 6:00.
Source: level1_curriculum/lesson9/Level1_Lesson9.md (Progress Check step; Student Pages: Progress Check; Answer key).
